provenance.selection_rationale: Galaxite is included from open primary crystal thermochemistry. Its Gibbs function uses the measured Cp fit and S°298.15; no primary formation enthalpy exists, so the assessed -39.5 kJ/mol oxide-formation value is used with ±12.6 kJ/mol uncertainty. Below fusion, the Tier 3 entropy and Cp spreads use the maximum measured residual among liquid-reference spinel homologues MgAl2O4 and Mg2TiO4 (N=2). The MgAl2O4 homologue now uses Shornikov (2017), Table 2, ΔfusH=55.81±4.62 kJ/mol at retained JANAF Al-090 Tm=2408 K, with JANAF Al-089 crystal and Al-090 liquid Cp. The class-C Tier-3 entropy and Cp leave-one-out columns and the updated homologue spread set the galaxite uncertainty envelope. The central galaxite Gibbs function remains derived from galaxite thermochemistry. No Chen activity data were used to choose the row. Held-out summary: all_three: median ratio 5.731, out-of-band 43/55; without_MnSiO3: median ratio 9.256, out-of-band 49/55; without_Mn2SiO4: median ratio 5.984, out-of-band 44/55; without_MnAl2O4: median ratio 7.168, out-of-band 49/55; MnSiO3_only: median ratio 7.573, out-of-band 49/55; Mn2SiO4_only: median ratio 14.489, out-of-band 51/55; MnAl2O4_only: median ratio 10.401, out-of-band 50/55; no_complexes: median ratio 17.023, out-of-band 52/55. rows.phase_or_construction: Composition-conditioned effective TiO1.5 bookkeeping species; not a unary Ti2O3(l) standard state.
rows.method: Evaluate Berry et al. (2024) equation 7 using the oxygen-weighted optical-basicity recipe, then map the reported Ti3+/Ti4+ ratio onto the TiO2-parent mass-action row.
rows.uncertainty_note: Berry et al. (2024) Table 1 (p. 212) reports the five measured-glass Lambda values as 0.5633-0.6345; recomputing from their reported oxide analyses with Berry’s oxygen-weighted definition and coefficients gives 0.5643-0.6353. The model uses that definition, including Berry’s TiO2 coefficient 1.10, and flags outside [0.5633,0.6353]. The glasses contain about 1.03 wt% TiO2 and were measured at 1673 K. The model assumes ideal Ti3+/Ti4+ mixing and Berry’s FMQ-parallel 6262.5/T slope. Across 73 held-out Tranell points (Lambda 0.6631-0.9079, 7.3-52.35 wt% TiO2, 1783-1903 K), all remain outside the Berry Lambda envelope; predictions under-predict Ti3+/Ti4+ by a median 0.5246 dex (maximum absolute residual 1.3300 dex). The basicity audit does not change predictions. Apollo 14072-like basalt (about 2.6 wt% TiO2, Lambda about 0.63) lies inside the Lambda envelope but above the 1.03 wt% anchor TiO2 content; high-Ti mare basalt (TiO2 > 6 wt% in the Neal & Taylor 1992 classification, GCA 56, 2177-2211) is well outside. The evidence does not establish an error onset between 1 and 7 wt% TiO2, so runtime flags begin above the 1.03 wt% anchor content.
range_flags: Berry equation 7 assumes ideal Ti3+/Ti4+ mixing and an FMQ-parallel 6262.5/T temperature slope.
